doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: What he hopes to be remembered for
summary: He says he wishes to be remembered as composing at his instrument, and discusses self-evaluation.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I guess at this point we can wrap. Do you have anything else that you’d like to tell future generations about yourself? Your music? Your legacy? What do you think you’ve, if you want people to remember you for anything in particular musically, what do you think that would be?

That I was willing and able, at times, to compose on my instrument. I haven’t been able to compose [or] orchestrate in that sense. I’ve always felt badly about that but I could improvise at times. I could then listen to it, that was always important to me, that I could listen to it after the fact and divorce myself from it to a large extent and hear it objectively as music and not just me playing the saxophone. That basically is my, I think, most accomplished musical practice so I identify with that.
Do you find self-evaluation easier now than it was, say, fifty years ago?

Yeah. I think so. Being drug-free helps that a lot. All the validation that [I] have had as a result of these efforts certainly helped my confidence. I’m very grateful for that. Just having the opportunity to do it this long is really a blessing.
Thank God and “knock on wood” that you’re now eighty-three, you’re still in good health, and you’re still playing great and people still want to hear you.

When I ever call Carl Berger I say “How you doing Carl?” He says, “I’m still tryin’ “. That’s a good line. I kind of like that. I appreciate the interest in trying to get this together. I wish I was a story-teller so I could make this more a “story-telling” thing. Somehow all those things are just passing fancies. All the gigs I play people say “Don’t you remember you played here?” No I don’t remember that because we went in and out the next morning to go to the next place and things like that. The record dates were almost like that many times; just like a little concert. I’m so pleased that you are reminding me of all of these things.
